messages.author: bd18ad1e33b09264
messages.subject: Problem with coord_trans and geom_*line
parts:
Hi

I'm having trouble adding vertical and horizontal to a plot that uses
a transformed coordinate system.
When I run the following code, I can see the lines in the first plot,
but they disappear in the second plot. I don't really understand why
this is happening. Am I doing something wrong?

require(ggplot2)
data <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = exp(0:9))
ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() +
geom_hline(yintercept = 9) + geom_vline(xintercept = 2)
last_plot() + coord_trans(y = 'log')

Running this code produces the error message
In match.fun(get(".transform", .))(values) : NaNs produced

I appended the output of sessionInfo() below. Prior to this version
the vertical lines used to not cover the whole range of the plot (I
guess the endpoints of the segments were not transformed correctly).
But after updating to 0.8.7 the lines have disappeared completely.

I could also use
ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() +
geom_hline(yintercept = 9) + geom_vline(xintercept = 2) +
scale_y_log()
but then I have the problem that I have to calculate breaks and labels
that look equally nice myself. My attempt in doing this produced
output that was not really satisfactory...

Thanks for the great package and for your time.
Regards,

Manuel

messages.subject: Re: Problem with coord_trans and geom_*line
parts:
Hi

geom*line sets -Inf for the start point, but log(-Inf) is NaN.
The codes below may generate what you want, although there may be side effects.

library(ggplot2)

GeomVline$draw <- function(., data, scales, coordinates, ...) {
data$y <- if(coordinates$objname=="trans" &&
coordinates$ytr$objname%in%c("log")) 0 else -Inf
data$yend <- Inf
GeomSegment$draw(unique(data), scales, coordinates)
}
GeomHline$draw <- function(., data, scales, coordinates, ...) {
data$x <- if(coordinates$objname=="trans" &&
coordinates$xtr$objname%in%c("log")) 0 else -Inf
data$xend <- Inf
GeomSegment$draw(unique(data), scales, coordinates)
}
Coord$munch_group <- function(., data, details, npieces=50) {
n <- nrow(data)
if(n==2 && (all(data$x==c(-Inf,Inf)) || all(data$y==c(-Inf,Inf)))) npieces=1
x <- approx(data$x, n = npieces * (n - 1) + 1)$y
y <- approx(data$y, n = npieces * (n - 1) + 1)$y
cbind(
.$transform(data.frame(x=x, y=y), details),
data[c(rep(1:(n-1), each=npieces), n), setdiff(names(data), c("x", "y"))]
)
}

data <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = exp(0:9))
ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() + geom_hline(yintercept = 9) +
geom_vline(xintercept = 2)
last_plot() + coord_trans(y = 'log')

messages.subject: Re: Problem with coord_trans and geom_*line
parts:
Hi

Your code seems to work alright! Thank you very much. Sometimes I use
sqrt instead of log, so to get this to work I just modified the if-
condition:

coordinates$xtr$objname%in%c("log", "sqrt"))

Thank you and have a nice day

Manuel

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Problem with coord_trans and geom_*line
parts:
Thanks for this quick fix. I think the long-term solution is for
coord_trans not transform infinite values. I've added a new bug to
this effect: http://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/issue/89

Hadley
